issue_context.title: lightning logical mode import should support persistent connection pooling and prepared statement and client statement cache
issue_context.body:
## Enhancement
during the tidb mode import, seems lightning destroy the connection after the insert, making it impossible to reuse the connection and plan cache hit.

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/aba317ae-7ac9-47c6-8993-93f51b0dfa91)

high overhead on sql parse and compile
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dcd11f02-b90d-4ce0-9ca0-384591fb4c14)

review_comments: (I'm not sure why the `kvcache.Key` interface call it `Hash`. Hash means a fixed-length digest)
please add a integration test for it
does the test of TestAdjustLogicalImportPrepStmt look good to you?
please add a integration test, ut it not enough for new features that's visible to user
please add it to `tidb-lightning.toml`

@alastori ptal, this PR will add new config

i think we can make prepared statement the default strategy, so no need this config
I prefer keep the config, in case we need to fallback to raw query.
please add it to tidb-lightning.toml
I think we don't need to check nilness. We have make sure it's not nil  when `err` is nil
If I remove the nilness check, the unit test failed, not sure why https://do.pingcap.net/jenkins/blue/organizations/jenkins/pingcap%2Ftidb%2Fghpr_unit_test/detail/ghpr_unit_test/17153/pipeline
Sorry we have a failpoint that returns (nil, nil)
should I get back the check `if db != nil `?
yes, sorry for my previous comment
you can init `values` of size len(row) here
Why not enable this by default?

```suggestion
```
as long as the table is importing, the prepared stmt is needed, no need such LRU

The reason to use LRU here is that the batch insert prepared statement may not be the same. where the insert/replace statement is constrained by `logical-import-batch-size` , the actual SQL executed might be longer or shorter, depending on the actual content imported.
depends on row size is unstable for prepared stmt, in worse case, every prepared stmt is different. we can ignore batch-size in this case, and only honors batch-rows, cc @lance6716
the default `logical-import-batch-rows` is 65536, usually this batch size is too large, should we lower the default value of `logical-import-batch-rows` to some reasonable number like 128/256/512?

Maybe we can ask the user that request this feature what's the root cause https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/issues/46607 . If the prepared statement can solve that problem, we can ignore these configurations. @D3Hunter and I are busy this week, please help to contact the issue author.

Not the author of #46607, but we've got customer which database is unable to handle 96 KB transactions thus requiring the limit to be lowered.

The `-batch-size` does not need to be very precise. It is mainly used to ensure (number of rows) × (size of row) to be maintained at a constant limit. You should *not* ignore the batch-size entirely because the same limit is shared among all tables and the constraint should be reasonable for both wide and narrow tables.
